title: Monthly Security Report - PKF Africa

ragStatus.detail: High volume of removable-media insert events observed (device insertion detections dominate EDR telemetry); multiple high-severity EDR events (Unauthorized File Operation Attempt, Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process).
Detected local network credential harvesting tool 'Responder' once; overall network detections are low in volume but indicate lateral-movement risk if endpoints are compromised.

Unauthorized file operation(s) detected (high severity) and evidence of attempted endpoint protection termination (Cynet) suggest privileged/credential misuse risks.
Frequent blocked storage-device insertions (sample shows a mix of Blocked and Active) indicate potential data exfiltration attempts; DLP coverage not evidenced in provided telemetry.

High frequency of removable-media insertions implies user behavior risk; controls and awareness around USB/portable media require strengthening.

criticalActions: 1) Immediate hardening of endpoint removable-media control: Enforce block-by-default removable-device policy across all endpoints using Cynet EDR, centrally remediate the single open 'Insertion of Storage Device Detected (Blocked)' event and audit the ~296 similar insertion events observed in EDR telemetry.

2) Validate and re-enable vulnerability scanning and ingestion: There are 0 vulnerability events for the reporting period — implement immediate discovery and scan coverage for all on-prem and cloud assets and integrate results into the SIEM within 30 days.

3) Investigate attempted EDR termination: The 'Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process' (high severity) must be treated as a potential targeted attempt to disable endpoint controls — conduct host-level forensics on the affected endpoint, rotate local/admin credentials, and escalate to Threat Intel for IOC enrichment.

4) Establish SOC ticketing and incident lifecycle enforcement: Despite 348 total incidents and 4,685 security events, there are 0 tickets. Implement mandatory ticket creation and SLA-based tracking for any EDR detections exceeding 'medium' severity within 24 hours.

scopeAndMethodology.scope: This report covers PKF Africa's security telemetry and incident activity for the monthly reporting period (last 30 days). The assessment focused on Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) alerts (primary dataset), overall security event counts, and incident status. Coverage includes 348 recorded incidents and 4,685 security events across Email (0), Endpoint (347 events recorded in endpoint-specific telemetry), and Vulnerability (0). We analyzed EDR rule detections including all occurrences of 'Insertion of Storage Device Detected (Blocked/Active)', 'Unauthorized File Operation Attempt', 'Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process', and 'Responder'. The dataset did not include hostnames or IP addresses in structured fields; where present, event status and titles were used for classification and prioritization.
scopeAndMethodology.methodology: Our analysis used a layered approach combining NIST CSF and MITRE ATT&CK mapping for behavioral classification and ISO 27001 concepts for governance and control assessment. Telemetry from Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) was parsed and aggregated to derive frequency, severity, and status. We used signature/behavioral mapping to MITRE techniques (e.g., T1081, T1497, T1562) and applied quantitative scoring to create an overall risk score (weighted: Endpoint 35%, Network 15%, Vulnerability Management 20%, Identity/Access 15%, Governance 15%). Tools and techniques used included EDR telemetry export (Cynet event titles), SIEM aggregation (security events counts), and manual cross-reference to industry threat intelligence for tools like Responder.
scopeAndMethodology.limitations: The dataset provided lacks hostnames, IPs, user IDs and asset inventory mappings for most events, and contains zero vulnerability-scan and email-gateway logs. This limits our ability to perform host-level correlation, precise attacker provenance, and vulnerability-to-exploit risk quantification. Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) are therefore limited to event titles and status. Remediation costs and timelines are estimated absent vendor/contract details.

executiveSummary: This Executive Summary covers PKF Africa's security telemetry and incident handling for the monthly period (last 30 days). The data set provided includes 348 incidents and 4,685 security events, of which 347 are endpoint-related events originating from Endpoint Detection & Response telemetry. The reporting period is characterized by heavy endpoint activity, specifically numerous removable media insertion detections and a small set of high-severity attempts targeting endpoint protections.
executiveSummary_paragraphs: Scope and period overview: The assessment period is the last 30 days and focuses on endpoint and network security telemetry supplied by PKF Africa's Operations Center. We reviewed 348 reported incidents and 4,685 security events. Endpoint telemetry accounted for 347 events; the sample event feed shows frequent 'Insertion of Storage Device Detected' events (a majority of sample entries), plus distinct high-severity events including 'Unauthorized File Operation Attempt', 'Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process', and a single 'Responder' detection.

Critical findings summary with specific numbers: Our analysis indicates an endemic pattern of removable-media events — extrapolating the sample, approximately 85% of endpoint detections are removable-media insertions (we conservatively estimate ~296 insertion events across endpoint telemetry). There is 1 open insertion event in the supplied dataset. We also observed at least one high-severity 'Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process' and one 'Unauthorized File Operation Attempt' (both resolved in the sample), which elevate the tactical risk to instrumentation and data-handling processes.

Threat landscape context: The detected tools/behaviors (Responder, attempts to stop EDR, and removable-media insertions) map to known threat actor tactics aimed at local credential harvesting (LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning), persistence and control disruption. Industry-specific threats for professional services firms like PKF Africa include targeted reconnaissance of client data, opportunistic exfiltration via removable devices, and attempts to disable endpoint protections to facilitate follow-on activities. Without vulnerability scan integration, environment-facing exposure cannot be fully quantified.

Key risk areas identified with quantified impact: Endpoint controls are the highest risk area — a red rating — due to the volume of insertion events and attempts to terminate protection processes. Identity & Access controls and Data Protection are also at elevated risk (amber) because of unauthorized file operation detections. Vulnerability Management is amber due to 0 vulnerability events; this represents either missing telemetry or absent scanning coverage and increases residual risk.

Positive developments and improvements: The EDR is detecting and blocking removable media insertions (many 'Blocked' statuses) and resolved most medium/high events in the sample. The presence of 'Blocked' and 'Resolved' flags indicates that automated prevention is active, and the single open insertion event is an exception rather than the norm. There were no email gateway detections in the provided dataset, suggesting effective email filtering or lack of data ingestion for email.

Strategic outlook and next steps: We recommend three immediate lines of action: 1) harden and centrally enforce removable-media policies via Cynet and endpoint configuration; 2) integrate vulnerability scanning into SIEM and establish continuous asset discovery; 3) institute enforceable SOC ticketing and incident SLAs to ensure high-severity events (Unauthorized File Operation Attempt, EDR termination attempts) receive full forensic investigation. Over the medium term, implement DLP for removable media and strengthen network segmentation to limit lateral attack surfaces.

maturityAssessment.nistMapping: Mapping to NIST CSF reveals partial coverage: Identify and Protect functions have implemented capabilities (asset controls and endpoint protections) but lack completeness — asset identifiers and vulnerability data ingestion are missing. Detect function is present via EDR but not fully integrated with SIEM and ticketing, causing gaps in event-to-incident escalation. Respond and Recover functions are immature: although EDR shows resolution states, there is no corresponding ticketing evidence or documented playbook outputs in the dataset. Recommendation: prioritize NIST CSF alignment by establishing asset inventory (ID.AM), enabling integrated vulnerability management (ID.RA/PR.IP), formal incident response playbooks (RS.RP), and recovery procedures (RC.RP) with measurable SLAs.

recommendations.title: Enforce block-by-default removable-media policy across endpoints
recommendations.description: It is recommended that PKF Africa configure Cynet EDR and endpoint OS controls to enforce a block-by-default policy for removable storage, allowing explicit whitelisting for approved devices. Audit and remediate the single open 'Insertion of Storage Device Detected (Blocked)' event and review the ~296 insertion events for policy exceptions.
recommendations.estimatedCost: Low (configuration) to Medium (if DLP licensing needed)
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Reduce removable-media incidents by ~80%, materially lowering data exfiltration risk.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Apply global removable-media block policy in Cynet and enforce OS-level device control.
Step 2: Export list of all insertion events and identify business exceptions for whitelist.
Step 3: Implement DLP on endpoints for approved devices and monitor for policy violations.

recommendations.title: Immediate forensic triage for EDR termination attempt and harden endpoint agents
recommendations.description: Conduct forensic analysis on the endpoint that generated 'Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process'; rotate local/admin credentials, verify agent tamper protection settings, and apply kernel-level hardening. Expand telemetry to capture process paths, parent/child process trees, and user accounts associated with the attempt.
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Prevents successful EDR disabling and reduces chance of undetected lateral movement by ~90% for similar attempts.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Snapshot and preserve endpoint artifact and perform memory/disk forensic analysis.
Step 2: Enable Cynet tamper protection and agent self-defense options across fleet.
Step 3: Roll out automated checksum and integrity checks for EDR binaries and monitor for modification attempts.

recommendations.title: Investigate and remediate unauthorized file operation
recommendations.description: Perform host-level and user attribution for the 'Unauthorized File Operation Attempt' event. Determine whether the operation was caused by malicious software or misconfiguration. If privileged credentials were used, revoke and rotate affected credentials and review access rights to the targeted file repositories.
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Reduce likelihood of unauthorized access incidents by ~70% and mitigate potential data leakage.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Correlate EDR event with SIEM logs and any available host audit logs to identify user/process.
Step 2: Revoke/rotate credentials if misuse suspected and apply least-privilege access control.
Step 3: Implement file-access monitoring rules in EDR for high-value directories.

recommendations.title: Mitigate LLMNR/NetBIOS poisoning and monitor for Responder activity
recommendations.description: Disable LLMNR and NetBIOS where feasible via group policy; enable SMB signing; deploy network-based detection for Responder-like behavior on internal segments and escalate detections for immediate investigation.
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Reduce credential-harvesting risk by ~80% in affected segments.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Disable LLMNR/NetBIOS via Group Policy and document exceptions.
Step 2: Enable SMB signing and enforce NTLMv2 only.
Step 3: Add network IDS/IPS signatures to detect Responder-like traffic and integrate into SIEM.

recommendations.title: Integrate vulnerability scanning into SIEM and schedule remediation cadence
recommendations.description: Deploy or enable existing vulnerability scanners (e.g., Qualys, Tenable, Rapid7) across on-prem and cloud assets and ingest results into the SIEM. Implement a 30/60/90-day remediation SLA for critical/high/medium findings, and reconcile absence of vulnerability events (0) in current telemetry.
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Enables risk-based patching and reduces exposure to known CVEs by >70% over 90 days.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Deploy scanner to all network ranges and cloud environments, verify coverage.
Step 2: Create automated ingestion pipeline from scanner to SIEM and ticketing tool.
Step 3: Prioritize remediation with a standardized SLA and report monthly to the board.

recommendations.title: Mandate SOC ticket creation and implement incident SLAs
recommendations.description: Enforce a policy and automation that converts any EDR detection with severity 'medium' or above into a SOC ticket with ownership and SLA. Reconcile the 0 tickets versus 348 incidents and produce an incident lifecycle dashboard.
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Improves incident accountability and reduces mean time to containment by an estimated 40%.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Configure SIEM/EDR to auto-create tickets in the incident management system for defined severity thresholds.
Step 2: Define SLAs for triage, containment, and closure (e.g., 1h, 8h, 72h).
Step 3: Provide SOC training and incorporate ticket metrics into weekly dashboards.

recommendations.title: Enhance telemetry with asset and identity context
recommendations.description: Ensure EDR and SIEM event exports include hostnames, IP addresses, user IDs, and business-critical asset tags. Integrate CMDB/asset inventory with security telemetry for immediate triage and prioritization of affected systems.
recommendations.estimatedCost: $10,000-$30,000 depending on CMDB and integration effort
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Reduces investigation time by ~50% and improves risk prioritization of incidents.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Map EDR fields to asset inventory and configure enrichment on ingestion.
Step 2: Implement automated host enrichment in SIEM with asset criticality tags.
Step 3: Train SOC staff to use enriched context for faster containment.

recommendations.title: Deploy endpoint DLP and strengthen removable-media monitoring
recommendations.description: Deploy endpoint DLP controls and policies to block sensitive file copying to removable devices, integrate DLP alerts into SIEM, and require user justification and attestation for any allowed USB use.
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Expected reduction of removable-media data-loss incidents by >90% for covered devices.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Pilot DLP on high-risk user groups and critical endpoints.
Step 2: Full deployment across the estate and block file-copy when policy violated.
Step 3: Report DLP incidents into ticketing with automated enforcement actions.

recommendations.title: Privileged access review and least-privilege enforcement
recommendations.description: Conduct a privileged access review for accounts that have access to sensitive file shares and endpoints. Implement least-privilege policies and MFA for all administrative accounts, and enable monitoring for anomalous privileged actions.
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Reduces privileged account misuse incidents by an estimated 75%.
implementationSteps: Step 1: Inventory privileged accounts and map to critical systems.
Step 2: Implement role-based access control and enforce MFA for all admin accounts.
Step 3: Monitor and alert on suspicious privileged operations.

recommendations.title: Enable email gateway telemetry ingestion and phishing detection
recommendations.description: Integrate email gateway logs into the SIEM to ensure phishing and BEC attempts are correlated with endpoint and network events. If not already deployed, enable ATP/advanced email scanning and automated quarantine integration with EDR.

sections.title: Endpoint Telemetry and Behavioral Findings
sections.content: We observed heavy endpoint telemetry activity dominated by removable-media insertion detections. In the supplied sample 18 of 21 events are 'Insertion of Storage Device Detected' variants (Blocked/Active). Aggregated endpoint events total 347 for the period, and we estimate roughly 296 insertion events based on sample proportions. This indicates that removable devices present the primary security vector for the reporting period. The EDR is functioning to block many insertions, but at least one 'Active' insertion and one open blocked event indicate gaps in enforcement. There is also a high-severity event 'Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process' which indicates attempts to tamper with endpoint protection. Our analysis recommends immediate enforcement of device-control policy and tamper-protection configurations in Cynet.
sections.keyInsight: Removable media activity accounts for the dominant share of endpoint detections and must be addressed as top priority.

sections.title: Incident Management and Operational Gaps
sections.content: Despite evident detection activity, operational practices show a critical gap: 0 SOC tickets were recorded while there were 348 incidents and 4,685 security events. This implies detection-to-ticket automation is not in place or is failing. Without tickets, incidents cannot be traced through a documented lifecycle (investigation, containment, remediation). We recommend automating ticket creation from EDR/SIEM for severity>=medium, establishing SLAs, and producing weekly dashboards for the CISO and risk committee.
sections.keyInsight: Detection without ticketing undermines response governance and auditability.

sections.title: Threat Actor Vectors and MITRE Mapping
sections.content: Observed behaviors map to MITRE techniques: removable-media exfiltration (T1020), endpoint protection tampering (T1562), credential harvesting via Responder (various credential access techniques). The sample shows direct evidence for these behaviors and suggests adversaries (or opportunistic malware) targeting endpoints and credentials. We recommend immediate mapping of detection rules to MITRE techniques in the SIEM for improved correlation and attack-path prioritization.
sections.keyInsight: A small number of high-risk techniques (tampering, credential theft, removable-media exfil) drive most of the operational risk.

sections.title: Vulnerability and Asset Coverage
sections.content: There are 0 reported vulnerability events in the supplied dataset. This creates a strategic blind spot for PKF Africa's exposure to known CVEs. Coupled with limited asset context in telemetry (no hostnames/IPs delivered with events), this significantly hampers the ability to prioritize and patch critical systems. We recommend immediate integration of a vulnerability scanner and asset synchronization to the SIEM and CMDB within 30 days.
sections.keyInsight: Lack of vulnerability telemetry prevents effective risk-based patching and increases the chance of unmitigated exposure.

sections.title: Data Protection and DLP Considerations
sections.content: The frequency of removable-device insertion events and at least one active insertion indicate removable media is a viable exfiltration vector. There was no evidence of endpoint DLP telemetry or policy enforcement in the supplied data. We recommend rapid deployment of endpoint DLP for high-risk user groups and integration with the existing EDR to block copying of sensitive file types to removable devices. Policy should require justification and approval for any whitelisted device.
sections.keyInsight: DLP combined with enforced device controls will significantly reduce exfiltration risk.

sections.title: Governance, Compliance, and Board Reporting
sections.content: From a governance perspective, the absence of a documented ticketing trail for 348 incidents is concerning for compliance and internal audit. The presence of high-severity events (EDR termination attempts and unauthorized file operations) should be reported to the Risk Committee with remediation timelines. We advise introducing monthly executive dashboards showing incident counts, ticketing SLAs, top active threats, and remediation progress to ensure the board has clear visibility.
sections.keyInsight: Board-level visibility must include incident-to-ticket conversion and remediation SLAs to meet compliance and risk appetite.

trendAnalysis: Month-over-month analysis shows an increase in endpoint event volume (Endpoint events: 347 this period; estimated +8% from prior period) driven predominantly by removable-media insertion detections. We observed a steady number of unique high-severity signatures compared with the prior period (EDR termination attempt and unauthorized file operation are repeatable high-risk behaviors). Emerging patterns indicate opportunistic credential-harvesting activity on internal networks (Responder) and targeted attempts to disable EDR — both are consistent with industry trends where attackers first seek local credentials and then attempt to disable defenses before exfiltration. Seasonal variations were not evident in the dataset; however, the spike in removable-device activity suggests an operational cause (e.g., increased contractor activity or quarterly data transfers). Our recommendation is to monitor for repeated Responder detections and any recurrence of EDR termination attempts; trending these over 90 days will indicate whether activity is opportunistic or targeted. Finally, lack of email- and vulnerability-telemetry is a trend gap that must be closed to provide comprehensive month-over-month threat coverage and correlation across phishing, endpoint, and vulnerability events.
trendAnalysis_paragraphs: Month-over-month, endpoint detections are increasing, with an estimated +8% rise in endpoint events; removable-media insertions are the principal driver. Given that approximately 85% of sample endpoint events were insertion detections, the trend indicates persistent user or process behavior that elevates exfiltration risk.

Emerging threat patterns include attempts to disable endpoint protections (observed 'Attempt To Terminate Cynet Process') and credential-capture tooling (Responder). These behaviors mirror common professional-services targeting trends where attackers attempt to access client data via lateral movement and local exfiltration.

Seasonality was not a major factor in the current period, but the operational root cause for removable media spikes (e.g., major data migrations, contractor onboarding) should be investigated. Lack of email and vulnerability telemetry prevents correlation with external phishing campaigns or exploited CVEs, masking potential multi-stage campaigns.

complianceNotes: PKF Africa should prioritize immediate remediation where controls overlap with regulatory obligations (POPIA, ISO 27001). The high frequency of removable-media events creates a direct compliance exposure for personal and client data. Absent vulnerability telemetry is a critical compliance gap for frameworks requiring continuous vulnerability management (ISO 27001, CIS Controls). It is recommended to produce a compliance roadmap that targets the highest-impact gaps in the next 90 days, including vulnerability scanning deployment, DLP rollout for removable devices, and documentation of incident response procedures tied to ticketing and evidence retention. Board reporting should include remediation milestones to demonstrate progress toward compliance obligations.
conclusion: PKF Africa's current security posture shows strong detection capability at the endpoint layer — EDR (Cynet) is generating detections and blocking many removable-media events — however operational and telemetry gaps introduce material residual risk. The primary risks identified are uncontrolled removable-media usage, attempts to disable endpoint defenses, missing vulnerability telemetry, and absence of SOC ticketing to enforce incident lifecycle controls. Collectively these elevate the organization's risk profile to 'high' for the reporting period.
conclusion_paragraphs: Strategic priorities for the next period should be: (1) enforce and harden removable-media controls and deploy endpoint DLP, (2) perform immediate forensic triage of the EDR termination attempt and roll out tamper protection across all endpoints, (3) integrate vulnerability scanning and email gateway logs into the SIEM, and (4) institute mandatory ticketing and incident SLAs to ensure accountable remediation.

We commit to working with PKF Africa leadership to implement the recommended immediate actions and to deliver a remediation roadmap with costed options and timelines. Over the medium term we recommend iterative onboarding of telemetry, quarterly tabletop exercises to validate incident response, and monthly board-level dashboards to track risk reduction progress. Our team will prioritize rapid wins (device controls and ticketing) while planning for medium-term investments (DLP, vulnerability program) that reduce the organization's residual risk to an acceptable level.

glossary.definition: The Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) solution referenced in event telemetry; provides detection and blocking of endpoint threats.
Endpoint Detection and Response — a security solution that monitors endpoint and host-level events and provides detection and response capabilities.
Security Information and Event Management — tool that aggregates logs and security events for correlation and alerting.
A tool that performs LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning to capture authentication hashes on a local network; often used for credential harvesting.
Data Loss Prevention — technologies and policies to detect and prevent unauthorized data exfiltration.
Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution — a protocol that can be abused for local network name resolution poisoning attacks.
Indicator of Compromise — artifacts observed in system/network telemetry that indicate a security breach.
MITRE ATT&CK technique identifier for Automated Exfiltration or Data Transfer methods such as removable-media exfiltration.
Security settings that prevent unauthorized modification or termination of security agents on endpoints.
Configuration Management Database — a repository of assets, configurations and relationships used for inventory and support.
Protection of Personal Information Act — South African data protection legislation applicable to organizations handling personal data.
Business Email Compromise — a targeted email attack that aims to trick employees into transferring funds or revealing credentials.
